summary: Coffee County, AL former lookout site administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission; the register says it stood where a water tank now stands, with no trace left.

facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites says no trace of the tower is left; the site is now a water tank

events.note: Registered September 15, 2019; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
tower was located where a water tank now stands
evidence.quote: Tower was located where this water tank is now.

evidence.supports: no trace of the tower is left
opinion piece: at one time over 200 towers dotted Alabama
evidence.quote: at one time, over 200 of these artifacts dotted Alabama

evidence.supports: most common explanation: aircraft watch a wider area than a tall tower
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide

evidence.supports: probably fewer than 75 still standing in Alabama
evidence.quote: there are probably less than 75 of these historic structures still standing in Alabama

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLOS register entry describes this site. No build date, design, staffing or fire history was found. The water-tank detail rests on the register alone; no photo or second source was checked. Searches used: 2 (one websearch.py fallback, one WebSearch); the returned results were about Victoria, Australia, and an unrelated Limestone County tower. Kaufmann is a statewide opinion piece, used only for context.
